$comment: Source of truth for the Drill Library. Edit this file, run `pnpm mirror:drills` (uploads any non-blob URLs to Vercel Blob), `pnpm posters:drills` (first-frame posters for drills with posterUrl null), then `pnpm build:drills` (regenerates src/lib/drills.ts). Fields: id is the INTERNAL key — storage, Blob paths and every data structure use it, and it never appears in a public URL. slug is the PUBLIC URL segment (/drills/<sport>/<slug>), keyword-matching and seeded from the drill name in kebab-case with no sport prefix, because the sport is already its own path segment. A slug is IMMUTABLE once shipped: retitling a drill must NOT move its URL, so the slug lives here as its own field rather than being derived from the name at build time. Changing one is a redirect decision (add a 301 to next.config.ts and update the pinned list in src/lib/drill-seo.test.ts), never a quiet edit. clips.* may be a CloudFront source URL (gets mirrored) or an existing Blob URL (served as-is). posterUrl null means: generate a poster from the demo clip's first frame. durationSeconds is the MEASURED length of the demo clip, written by the ffprobe pass in mirror-drills.mjs — never hand-edited and never estimated; absent or null means it has not been measured and VideoObject then emits no duration at all. sourceCdn preserves the original CloudFront provenance of clips whose manifest URL is already a Blob URL. alternates are unused alternate takes, kept for reference only. sports maps every sport id (the lowercase value used in drills[].sport) to its display name and chip icon; add a sport here and it is fully supported — chips, icons, and counts all derive from this file, no code changes.
$contentComment: TEACHING CONTENT (summary, builds, equipment, space, steps, mistakes, trackedStat) is OPTIONAL on every drill and is the shared source for the in-app drill detail page and the future public drill pages. HARD RULE: this content is written by a human and copied verbatim. Never generate, infer, or paraphrase sports technique — a wrong detail here teaches a kid wrong form. A field that is absent is absent: the generator emits null and the UI renders no section at all rather than an empty one. Field shapes: summary string (2-3 plain sentences); builds string[] (2-4 short phrases); equipment string[] or ["none"]; space string (driveway | backyard | gym | field); steps [{ n int, title string, detail string }] with n starting at 1 and contiguous; mistakes [{ mistake string, fix string }]; trackedStat string naming the athlete stat-sheet key this drill improves, or null when no stat has been agreed for it (null everywhere today — the personal-best panel stays hidden until real stat keys are chosen).

coaches.name: Koach Amari
coaches.style: Handles and finishing. Reps until it's automatic.

coaches.name: Koach Nia
coaches.style: Close control and first touch. Small touches, big difference.

coaches.name: Koach Rio
coaches.style: Swing path and glove work. Clean reps only.

coaches.name: Koach Sol
coaches.style: Platform and hands. Control before power.

coaches.name: Koach Zuri
coaches.style: Sprint mechanics. Fast is a skill you practice.

coaches.name: Koach Marisol
coaches.style: Circle work and swings. Repeat it until it's yours.

drills.name: Crossover
drills.description: Snap the ball across your body and change direction.
drills.summary: A crossover is how you change direction fast. You push the ball low and quick from one hand to the other, and your whole body goes with it.

steps.title: Get low
steps.detail: Bend your knees into an athletic stance. The lower you are, the faster you can move.

steps.title: Dribble hard
steps.detail: Keep the ball below your knee. A low dribble is a fast dribble and it is much harder to steal.

steps.title: Push it across
steps.detail: Snap the ball across your body to your other hand. One bounce, close to the ground.

steps.title: Move your body
steps.detail: Your shoulders and hips go the same way as the ball. If only your hand moves, nobody is fooled.

steps.title: Go
steps.detail: Push off your outside foot and accelerate. A crossover only works if you actually go somewhere.

mistakes.fix: Keep the bounce below your knee.
Turn your shoulders and hips with the ball.
Pick a spot on the wall and keep your eyes up.

drills.name: Form shooting
drills.description: Build a clean shot from close range, one rep at a time.
drills.summary: Form shooting is shooting from close range so you can groove a clean, repeatable motion. It is not about scoring from far away. It is about making the exact same shot every time.

steps.title: Start close
steps.detail: Stand a step or two from the rim. You should barely need any power.

steps.title: Set your hand
steps.detail: Shooting hand under the ball, fingers spread. Your other hand is only a guide on the side.

steps.title: Elbow under
steps.detail: Line your shooting elbow up under the ball, not flared out to the side.

steps.title: Up and out
steps.detail: Push straight up and release at the top. Your legs give the power, not your arm.

steps.title: Hold the finish
steps.detail: Snap your wrist and hold your hand in the air until the ball lands. Fingers pointed at the rim.

mistakes.fix: The guide hand only rides along. Take it off right at release.
Tuck it in so it points at the rim.
Freeze the follow through on every single rep.

drills.name: Inside pass
drills.description: Pass with the inside of your foot for accuracy.
drills.summary: The inside of your foot is the most accurate surface you have. Almost every pass in a real game uses it. This drill builds a pass you can trust under pressure.

steps.title: Plant your foot
steps.detail: Put your non kicking foot beside the ball, toe pointed at your target.

steps.title: Turn your foot out
steps.detail: Open your kicking foot sideways so the flat inside surface faces where you are passing.

steps.title: Lock the ankle
steps.detail: Keep your ankle stiff. A loose ankle sends the ball anywhere it wants.

steps.title: Strike the middle
steps.detail: Hit the middle of the ball with the arch of your foot.

steps.title: Follow through
steps.detail: Keep your foot moving toward the target after contact.

mistakes.mistake: Plant foot pointed the wrong way
mistakes.fix: Point your toe exactly where you want the ball to go.
Use the flat inside of your foot, never the tip.
Do half your reps with your weak foot every session.

drills.name: First touch
drills.description: Cushion the ball so your next move is already set up.
drills.summary: Your first touch is what you do the instant the ball arrives. A good one sets up your next move. A bad one means you spend the next three seconds chasing.

steps.title: Get behind the ball
steps.detail: Move your feet so your body is in line with it. Do not reach for it.

steps.title: Pick your surface
steps.detail: Inside of the foot for most balls. Sole or thigh for balls coming in higher.

steps.title: Cushion it
steps.detail: As the ball arrives, pull your foot back slightly so it takes the pace off instead of bouncing away.

steps.title: Touch it where you are going
steps.detail: Push it into space in the direction you want to move, not straight down at your feet.

steps.title: Look up
steps.detail: Head up immediately after the touch so you can see what is in front of you.

mistakes.fix: Relax and give a little so the ball stays close.
Angle the touch into space so you can move onto it.
Move your feet to the ball instead of stretching for it.

drills.name: Tee work
drills.description: Groove your swing path off the tee.
drills.summary: The tee takes the pitch out of the equation so you can work on nothing but your swing. Every good hitter uses one, all the way up to the pros.

steps.title: Set the tee
steps.detail: Belt high to start, positioned out in front of your front hip.

steps.title: Take your stance
steps.detail: Feet a little wider than your shoulders, knees soft, hands back.

steps.title: Load
steps.detail: Small shift of weight back onto your back hip. Nothing dramatic.

steps.title: Swing through
steps.detail: Turn your back hip and let your hands follow. Swing through the ball, not at it.

steps.title: Finish balanced
steps.detail: End with your weight on your front side and your eyes still down where the ball was.

mistakes.fix: Start the swing with your hips and let your hands follow.
Adjust the height and focus on the top half of the ball.
Slow the swing down until you can finish under control.

drills.name: Ready position
drills.description: Get in an athletic stance before every pitch.
drills.summary: Ready position is what you do before every single pitch. Fielders who look fast are usually just the ones who started ready.

steps.title: Feet wide
steps.detail: A little wider than your shoulders.

steps.title: Bend your knees
steps.detail: Get your weight onto the balls of your feet, not back on your heels.

steps.title: Glove out front
steps.detail: Hands out in front of your body, glove open and low.

steps.title: Small hop
steps.detail: As the pitch reaches the plate, take a tiny hop so you land right as the ball is hit. This is what makes fielders quick.

steps.title: React
steps.detail: Push off in the direction of the ball on your very first step.

mistakes.fix: Get in your stance before the pitch, not after the ball is hit.
Stay on the balls of your feet so you can move either direction.
Keep them out front and ready.

drills.name: Catch triangle
drills.description: Palms out, thumbs and pointer fingers make a triangle. Catch with your hands, not your body.
drills.summary: Catching with your hands instead of your body is the difference between a receiver and everyone else. The triangle is how you make sure your hands get there first.

steps.title: Hands up
steps.detail: Bring both hands up in front of your face before the ball arrives.

steps.title: Make the triangle
steps.detail: Thumbs together and pointer fingers together so there is a triangle window between them.

steps.title: Palms out
steps.detail: Turn your palms toward the ball. You should be able to see the throw through the triangle.

steps.title: Catch the point
steps.detail: Let the front point of the ball come through the middle of the triangle and squeeze with your fingers.

steps.title: Tuck it away
steps.detail: Pull the ball into your body immediately after the catch.

steps.title: Low balls flip
steps.detail: For anything below your waist, flip your hands so your pinkies touch instead of your thumbs.

mistakes.fix: Reach out and catch with your hands away from your body.
Watch the ball all the way into your hands.
Turn your palms toward the ball so the triangle faces the throw.

drills.name: Three-point stance
drills.description: Low stance, flat back, head up. Explode out on the first step.
drills.summary: A three point stance is how linemen and a lot of skill players start every play. Done right, you are already moving forward before anyone else has reacted.

steps.title: Stagger your feet
steps.detail: Feet about shoulder width, one foot slightly behind the other.

steps.title: Squat down
steps.detail: Bend your knees and drop your hips. Do not bend at the waist.

steps.title: Hand down
steps.detail: Put one hand on the ground out in front, fingertips down, with only a little weight on it.

steps.title: Flat back, head up
steps.detail: Your back is flat like a tabletop and your eyes look forward, not down.

steps.title: Explode
steps.detail: Push off your back foot and drive out low and forward. Stay low for the first few steps.

mistakes.mistake: Too much weight on your hand
mistakes.fix: You should be able to lift the hand without falling. Keep the weight in your legs.
Drive out low. Standing up kills all your power.
Flatten your back and lift your eyes.

drills.name: Sprint start
drills.description: Stay low out of your stance and drive for the first steps.
drills.summary: Most races and almost every play start from a standing position. How you start decides a lot of what happens after.

steps.title: Stagger your feet
steps.detail: Strong foot forward, other foot about a shoe length back.

steps.title: Lean forward
steps.detail: Shift your weight over your front foot until you almost feel like you are falling.

steps.title: Load your arms
steps.detail: Opposite arm to your front leg, both elbows bent and ready.

steps.title: Drive out
steps.detail: Push hard off the front foot and drive your back knee forward.

steps.title: Stay low
steps.detail: Keep your body angled forward for the first five or six steps before you stand tall.

mistakes.fix: Hold the forward lean for five to six steps.
Drive your knee forward and cover ground.
Drive them straight forward and back.

drills.name: Arm drive
drills.description: Elbows at 90, hands cheek to pocket. Fast arms make fast legs.
drills.summary: Your arms set the rhythm your legs follow. Fast, clean arms make your legs faster without you having to think about them.

steps.title: Stand tall
steps.detail: Feet under your hips, chest up, shoulders relaxed.

steps.title: Bend to ninety
steps.detail: Both elbows bent at about a right angle, and keep them there the whole time.

steps.title: Cheek to pocket
steps.detail: Drive your hand up toward your cheek, then back down past your hip pocket.

steps.title: Straight lines
steps.detail: Arms move straight forward and back, never across your body.

steps.title: Stay loose
steps.detail: Hands relaxed, shoulders down. Tight shoulders make you slower.

mistakes.fix: Move them front to back like pistons.
Relax your hands and drop your shoulders.
Hold the ninety degree bend for the whole set.

drills.name: Two-ball dribbling
drills.description: Dribble two balls at once. Your weak hand gets a lot better, fast.
drills.summary: Dribbling two balls at once forces both hands to work at the same time. Your weak hand gets exposed fast, which is exactly the point.

steps.title: Get low
steps.detail: Athletic stance, knees bent, eyes up before you start.

steps.title: Start together
steps.detail: Dribble both balls at the same time, same height, below your waist.

steps.title: Find the rhythm
steps.detail: Twenty dribbles in sync. Keep the bounces matched to each other.

steps.title: Go alternating
steps.detail: Now dribble them opposite, one ball up while the other is down. This is the hard part.

steps.title: Stay in control
steps.detail: If you lose one, pick it up and reset. Control beats speed every time.

mistakes.fix: Eyes up. Feel the dribble instead of looking at it.
Stay low for the whole set, not just the start.
Slow and controlled first. Speed comes after control.

drills.name: Mikan drill
drills.description: Layups off both hands, back and forth under the rim.
drills.summary: The Mikan drill is one of the oldest finishing drills in basketball and it still works. It teaches you to score with both hands around the rim without having to think about it.

steps.title: Start under the rim
steps.detail: Stand directly under the basket facing the backboard.

steps.title: Right hand first
steps.detail: Step with your left foot and lay the ball in off the backboard with your right hand.

steps.title: Catch it clean
steps.detail: Grab the ball out of the net before it hits the ground.

steps.title: Switch sides
steps.detail: Step across with your right foot and lay it in left handed off the other side of the square.

steps.title: Keep going
steps.detail: Back and forth without stopping. Ten makes on each side.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the ball hit the ground
mistakes.fix: Catch it out of the net to keep the rhythm going.

mistakes.mistake: Using your strong hand on both sides
mistakes.fix: The whole point of this drill is your weak hand. Use it.
Stay close and go straight up.

drills.name: Cone dribbling
drills.description: Weave through cones with small touches. Keep the ball close.
drills.summary: Cone dribbling teaches your feet to make lots of small touches instead of a few big ones. Close control is what lets you keep the ball when defenders are close.

steps.title: Set up your cones
steps.detail: Five or six in a line, about two steps apart.

steps.title: Small touches
steps.detail: Weave through using the inside and outside of both feet. Try to touch the ball every step.

steps.title: Keep it close
steps.detail: The ball should never get more than one step away from you.

steps.title: Head up
steps.detail: Glance up between cones. You will never see a teammate while staring at your feet.

steps.title: Come back weak footed
steps.detail: Go through again leading with your weaker foot.

mistakes.fix: More touches, smaller ones. Aim for one per step.

mistakes.mistake: Only using the inside of your foot
mistakes.fix: Use the outside too. It is faster and it is what you will need in a game.
Move at a jog. Control at speed is the whole goal.

drills.name: Juggling
drills.description: Keep it off the ground. Start with two, then beat your record.
drills.summary: You will not juggle in a game, but juggling builds the touch you use in every game. It teaches your foot to be soft and your eyes to track the ball all the way in.

steps.title: Start with a bounce
steps.detail: Drop the ball, let it bounce once, then flick it up with your laces.

steps.title: Use your laces
steps.detail: Contact the flat top of your foot with your toe pulled up slightly.

steps.title: Small and soft
steps.detail: Keep the ball around waist height. Big kicks are much harder to control.

steps.title: Stay relaxed
steps.detail: Soft knees, loose ankle, small steps to stay underneath the ball.

steps.title: Count and beat it
steps.detail: Count your best, then go for one more. That is the whole game.

mistakes.fix: Little taps. Waist high is plenty.
Relax it so the ball does not fly off your foot.
Once you can do ten, start alternating feet.

drills.name: Tee drive
drills.description: Load the back hip and drive through the ball. Finish balanced.
drills.summary: Same tee, different focus. This one is about where your power actually comes from: your hips and your back side, not your arms.

steps.title: Set up
steps.detail: Tee out in front of your front hip, belt high.

steps.title: Load the back hip
steps.detail: Shift your weight back and coil slightly. Small move, big difference.

steps.title: Start with the hips
steps.detail: Turn your back hip toward the pitcher first, before your hands move at all.

steps.title: Hands follow
steps.detail: Let your hands come through the zone level, driving through the ball.

steps.title: Finish tall
steps.detail: Back foot turned, weight forward, balanced, eyes down where the ball was.

mistakes.fix: Hips lead, hands follow. Slow it down until you can feel the order.
Load back before you go forward. No load means no power.
Swing level through the ball instead of up at it.

drills.name: Ground balls
drills.description: Glove down, field it out front with two hands, step into the throw.
drills.summary: Fielding a ground ball cleanly is mostly about your feet and your position, not your glove. Get there early and the catch becomes easy.

steps.title: Ready position
steps.detail: Wide feet, knees bent, glove out front before the ball is ever hit.

steps.title: Move to the ball
steps.detail: Shuffle so your body is lined up with it. Do not reach sideways.

steps.title: Get low and wide
steps.detail: Butt down, glove on the ground out in front of you where you can see it.

steps.title: Two hands
steps.detail: Field it out front with your throwing hand right above the glove, ready to grab.

steps.title: Into the throw
steps.detail: Bring it to your chest, step toward your target, and throw.

mistakes.fix: Field it out in front where your eyes can follow it into the glove.
Get your butt down and your glove on the ground.
Move toward it. Waiting lets the ball play you instead.

drills.name: Forearm passing
drills.description: Flat platform, low stance. Let the ball come to you.
drills.summary: The forearm pass, or bump, is the first contact on almost every play. A good platform sends the ball where you want without you swinging at it.

steps.title: Ready stance
steps.detail: Feet wider than your shoulders, knees bent, weight forward on the balls of your feet.

steps.title: Build the platform
steps.detail: Put one hand inside the other, thumbs side by side pointing down, and straighten both arms.

steps.title: Move your feet
steps.detail: Get your body behind the ball. Move first, then pass.

steps.title: Angle, do not swing
steps.detail: Point your platform where you want the ball and let it rebound off.

steps.title: Push with your legs
steps.detail: If you need more power, straighten your legs. Never swing your arms for it.

mistakes.fix: Hold the platform still and let the ball bounce off it.
Lock your arms straight so the surface stays flat.
Move your feet so the ball comes to your middle.

drills.name: Overhead setting
drills.description: Hands make a window above your forehead. Push with your legs.
drills.summary: Setting is the softest and most precise touch in volleyball. Your hands make a window and the ball goes exactly where you point them.

steps.title: Get under it
steps.detail: Move so the ball is dropping onto your forehead, not out in front of you.

steps.title: Make the window
steps.detail: Hands above your forehead with thumbs and pointer fingers forming a triangle you can see through.

steps.title: Soft fingers
steps.detail: Contact with the pads of your fingers, never your palms. Quiet hands.

steps.title: Push through
steps.detail: Extend your legs and arms together toward your target.

steps.title: Finish pointing
steps.detail: End with arms extended and fingers pointed where the ball went.

mistakes.fix: Contact only with the pads of your fingers.

mistakes.mistake: Setting from in front of your face
mistakes.fix: Move your feet and get all the way underneath it.
Push with your legs at the same time.

drills.name: A-skip
drills.description: Knee up, toe up, land on the ball of your foot. Rhythm over speed.
drills.summary: The A-skip teaches your legs the exact pattern good sprinting uses, just slower so you can learn it. Almost every track team in the world starts practice with this.

steps.title: Stand tall
steps.detail: Chest up, shoulders relaxed, eyes forward.

steps.title: Drive one knee
steps.detail: Bring one knee up to about hip height with your toe pulled up toward your shin.

steps.title: Add a skip
steps.detail: Small hop on your ground foot as the knee comes up.

steps.title: Strike down
steps.detail: Bring the foot down underneath your hip, landing on the ball of your foot. Not out in front.

steps.title: Alternate
steps.detail: Switch legs and hold a steady bouncy rhythm for about twenty meters.

mistakes.mistake: Reaching your foot out in front
mistakes.fix: Land underneath your hip, not ahead of it.
Pull your toe up toward your shin.
Stay tall with a very slight forward lean.

drills.name: Bounding
drills.description: Big leaping strides. This is how you build a stronger push.
drills.summary: Bounding is exaggerated running where every step is a leap. It builds the power that makes your normal stride longer and stronger.

steps.title: Start jogging
steps.detail: A few easy steps to get moving before the first bound.

steps.title: Leap into it
steps.detail: Push hard off one foot and jump forward, not up.

steps.title: Drive the knee
steps.detail: Bring your lead knee up and forward as you travel through the air.

steps.title: Land and go
steps.detail: Land on the ball of your foot and immediately push off into the next bound.

steps.title: Keep it short
steps.detail: Six to eight bounds, then walk back. This is a hard drill, not a long one.

mistakes.fix: Aim your push forward down the track.
Quality over quantity. Stop the set as soon as your form gets sloppy.
Warm up first and bound on grass or a track. Your knees and ankles will thank you.

drills.name: Laces shooting
drills.description: Plant beside the ball and strike through the middle with your laces.
drills.summary: The laces shot is how you hit a ball hard. It is a completely different motion from a pass, and it depends on a clean plant foot and a locked ankle.

steps.title: Approach at an angle
steps.detail: Take a few steps at a slight angle to the ball rather than straight on.

steps.title: Plant beside it
steps.detail: Non kicking foot right next to the ball, toe pointed at your target.

steps.title: Point your toe down
steps.detail: Lock your ankle with your toe pointed down and strike with your laces.

steps.title: Hit the middle
steps.detail: Contact the middle of the ball to keep the shot low. Get under it and the ball flies over the goal.

steps.title: Land forward
steps.detail: Follow through so you land on your shooting foot, moving toward the target.

mistakes.fix: Keep your chest over the ball. Leaning back is why shots go over the bar.
Point your toe down and lock the ankle before you strike.

mistakes.mistake: Plant foot too far from the ball
mistakes.fix: Put it right beside the ball, not a step away.

drills.name: Sole rolls and pull-backs
drills.description: Roll it side to side, then pull it back and turn away.
drills.summary: Sole rolls and pull backs are how you change direction with the ball glued to your foot. They are the base of almost every move you will ever learn.

steps.title: Ball in front
steps.detail: Stand with the ball just in front of you, knees bent.

steps.title: Roll it across
steps.detail: Use the sole of one foot to roll the ball sideways to your other foot.

steps.title: Roll it back
steps.detail: Same thing in the other direction. Build a steady rhythm.

steps.title: Add the pull back
steps.detail: Put your sole on top of the ball, drag it backward, then turn and go with it.

steps.title: Lead with each foot
steps.detail: Run the whole pattern leading with your left, then your right.

mistakes.fix: Stay on the balls of your feet with your knees bent.
Light touches on top. Do not stand on it.
Both feet, every single set.

drills.name: Windmill pitching
drills.description: Full circle over the top, release past the hip, finish balanced.
drills.summary: The windmill is the softball pitching motion. Your arm makes one full circle beside your body and the ball leaves at the bottom, right as your hand passes your hip.

steps.title: Start on the rubber
steps.detail: Both feet on the pitching rubber, ball in your glove, hands together in front of you.

steps.title: Separate and step
steps.detail: Push off your back foot and stride forward as your hands separate.

steps.title: Swing the circle
steps.detail: Bring your arm straight up past your ear, over the top, and down behind you. It stays beside your body and never crosses your chest.

steps.title: Release at your hip
steps.detail: Let the ball go at the bottom of the circle as your hand passes your hip, and snap your wrist.

steps.title: Finish balanced
steps.detail: Land on your stride foot with your weight forward and your arm following through naturally.

mistakes.mistake: Arm crossing in front of your body
mistakes.fix: The circle stays flat beside you, like a wheel spinning next to your side.

mistakes.mistake: Releasing too early or too late
mistakes.fix: The ball leaves right at your hip. Early sends it high, late puts it in the dirt.
Pitching stresses your arm. Build up slowly over weeks and stop as soon as you feel tired.

drills.name: Soft toss
drills.description: Someone tosses from the side, you drive it into the net. Level swing.
drills.summary: Soft toss puts a moving ball in front of you without a full pitch. It is the step between tee work and hitting live pitching.

steps.title: Set up
steps.detail: Stand in your stance facing a net. Your partner kneels off to the side, slightly in front of you.

steps.title: Get the toss
steps.detail: Partner tosses underhand into your hitting zone, out in front of your front hip.

steps.title: Load as it comes
steps.detail: Small shift back as the ball is tossed. Be loaded before it arrives, not after.

steps.title: Swing level
steps.detail: Turn your hips and drive your hands through the ball on a level path.

steps.title: Finish and reset
steps.detail: Balanced finish, eyes on the contact point, then set up for the next one.

mistakes.mistake: Partner kneeling in front of the hitter
mistakes.fix: Always toss from the side, slightly in front, well clear of the swing path.
Slow down. One good swing beats five rushed ones.
Let it come to your hitting zone instead of lunging at it.
